title: Cardinals’ Mike LaFleur has ‘a lot of respect’ for Kyler Murray, but QB’s future is uncertain
content:
INDIANAPOLIS — Arizona Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort on Tuesday said that “all options are on the table” regarding Kyler Murray and the team’s future at quarterback.

“As it pertains to that position — as it pertains to every position on our team — we’re going to look at every avenue to improve, and we’re going to continue to go through our process with that,” Ossenfort said from the NFL combine.

The Cardinals have Murray, Jacoby Brissett and Kedon Slovis all under contract entering 2026. However, Murray, whom the team selected with the No. 1 pick in 2019, only played in five games last season because of a foot injury. By season’s end, his future with the organization was unclear.

New head coach Mike LaFleur, who also spoke at the combine, didn’t disclose details of the conversations he has had with Murray, but said he is familiar with the quarterback because of the times he faced him as an opposing coach in the NFC West. LaFleur spent seven seasons combined in the division, including four as an assistant coach with the San Francisco 49ers and three as offensive coordinator of the Los Angeles Rams.

“(Murray) was always a problem,” LaFleur said. “I know the defensive coordinators I worked with, (facing Murray) wasn’t a fun week for them. A lot of respect for him as a player.”

The younger brother of Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur, Mike helped lead a Rams offense that ranked first in the NFL in points per game, yards per game, yards per play and expected points added per play in 2025. Quarterback Matthew Stafford won the league’s MVP award, and an obvious first order of business for LaFleur and Ossenfort in Arizona is to straighten out that position for the Cardinals.

Brissett stepped in after Murray’s injury in 2025 and recorded a career-high 3,366 passing yards with 23 touchdowns to eight interceptions. But the Cardinals went 1-11 with him as a starter and finished 3-14 overall. Ossenfort said he has always had “good dialogue” with Murray and that they shared in the disappointment in how the 2025 season played out.

“I’d say it wasn’t up to what Kyler wanted, it wasn’t up to what any one of us wanted as a season as a whole,” Ossenfort said. “When you have the kind of year we had, there’s a lot of room for improvement. We gotta find a way to do that not only at that position, and all positions.”

Asked if he would be open to playing a rookie quarterback in 2026, LaFleur said: “I’m open and embracing playing the best quarterback possible for the Arizona Cardinals. We’re still working through that process right now, and there’s going to be a lot of factors that lead into that.”
